incidents.vector: Intrusion largely driven by an autonomous open-source AI agent running in unrestricted mode, using web shells, HTTP tunnels, privilege-escalation exploits and a custom cross-platform backdoor.
incidents.impact: Multiple ministry systems compromised for reconnaissance, credential theft and network mapping, including enumeration of personnel records; no evidence of data exfiltration. Thai authorities were notified and the ministry has not publicly acknowledged the incident.

incidents.attacker: Criminal hacker — data theft and sale
incidents.vector: Compromise of an employee email account gave unauthorized access to internal data, later advertised for sale on a darknet marketplace.
incidents.impact: Actor claims to have taken customer information, corporate banking records, internal emails, loan documents and audit files from the Indian state-owned bank; the bank says core banking systems were not accessed and the incident is contained. Authenticity of the leaked data is unverified.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion into the foreign ministry's diplomat training system that persisted roughly ten months before discovery.
incidents.impact: Email addresses of diplomatic officials were leaked; South Korea is changing the email addresses of all diplomatic officials due to spear-phishing concerns.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-16723) in the Fastjson 1.x Java library, which works in its default configuration and common Spring Boot deployments.
incidents.impact: Ongoing attacks against Java applications across finance, healthcare, technology and retail, mostly in the US; no patch is available and Alibaba advises enabling SafeMode or migrating to the 2.x branch.

incidents.victim: Exiled Belarusian activist and regional Telegram users
incidents.vector: Highly personalized Telegram phishing using fake security alerts and per-target links to steal one-time login codes and hijack accounts.
incidents.impact: At least 64 targeted phone numbers identified across Belarus, Russia and Kazakhstan in a campaign active since late 2024; the reported target recognized the lure and no confirmed compromises were documented.

incidents.vector: Malware-driven network disruption; entry method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Phone and internet outages across all facilities forced closure of dozens of clinics and departments including imaging, OBGYN and primary care; urgent care remains open while systems are restored and patients are redirected in coordination with EMS and regional hospitals.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached a supplier and pivoted into a shared platform.
incidents.impact: Swiss train manufacturer held to a roughly $12.3 million ransom demand; the company says it will not pay.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed security breach under investigation.
incidents.impact: Australian energy provider investigating potential exposure of customer data; disclosed via ASX filing.

incidents.vector: Breach of company systems followed by misuse of stolen customer information.
incidents.impact: Stolen customer data used to fraudulently rent furniture and electronics on the Acima marketplace; fraudulent loan agreements estimated at around $13 million.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed breach; the company is notifying affected customers.
incidents.impact: Exposure of customer data including the last four digits of payment cards; customer notifications issued.

incidents.vector: Exploited a smart contract handling cross-chain transactions.
incidents.impact: Nearly $10 million in crypto assets stolen from the bridge in roughly eight minutes.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained some of the bridge's private keys and signed fraudulent withdrawal transactions.
incidents.impact: $24 million in cryptocurrency stolen from the platform.

incidents.victim: Zimbra webmail users (US, allied government and commercial networks)
incidents.vector: Phishing emails exploiting a stored cross-site scripting zero-day (CVE-2025-66376) that triggers when a victim simply views the message in vulnerable Zimbra webmail.
incidents.impact: Theft of credentials, session tokens, backup 2FA codes and the last 90 days of mailbox contents across government, defense, transportation and financial targets in NATO states, Ukraine and beyond since mid-2025; NSA, CISA, FBI and over a dozen allied agencies issued a joint advisory, and unpatched servers are still being exploited.

incidents.vector: Re-exploitation of the same unfixed smart contract function abused in the platform's May 2026 hack, by a different attacker.
incidents.impact: $7.5 million in Ether stolen; the platform's second theft this year after an $11.5 million loss in May.

incidents.vector: Spam email and voice phishing lead victims to install a fake Windows update that loads an in-memory remote access trojan using browser-based covert command-and-control channels.
incidents.impact: Ransomware-as-a-service operation gains covert remote control that evades network detection, then deploys double-extortion ransomware; ransom notes confirmed in observed intrusions.

incidents.vector: Chaining of two WordPress vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030) to achieve remote site takeover, with mass exploit attempts starting about three days after disclosure.
incidents.impact: Millions of WordPress sites exposed to remote takeover; widespread exploitation attempts observed across the internet.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (water, energy, government facilities)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of misconfigured internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (Rockwell, Schneider Electric, Siemens) using the manufacturers' own programming software to push malicious project files and ladder logic.
incidents.impact: Disrupted PLC function and manipulated HMI/SCADA displays across several US sectors since March; some victims saw operational disruption and financial loss, and safety-limiting logic was overridden at one victim. CISA updated its advisory with new detection guidance.

incidents.vector: Gift cards obtained through romance fraud, elder fraud, hacking and theft were used to buy high-value electronics reshipped to China, coordinated over WeChat with cryptocurrency payments.
incidents.impact: Federal grand jury indicted a Chinese national in New Hampshire for conspiracy to commit wire fraud in the international scheme; victims span multiple US states.

incidents.vector: Compromise of an investor portal gave unauthorized access to customer data.
incidents.impact: Investor data exposed, prompting a Thai Securities and Exchange Commission investigation; trading, settlement and depository systems were not affected.

incidents.vector: Compromise linked to a self-propagating worm in malicious npm packages, followed by theft and public dumping of internal files.
incidents.impact: Leaked source code and internal documents allegedly show large-scale scraping of songs and lyrics from YouTube Music, Deezer, Genius and other platforms, adding fuel to ongoing copyright lawsuits.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the certificate authority, newly attributed by researchers to a financially motivated group operating out of China.
incidents.impact: Compromise of a major certificate authority carries trust and PKI supply-chain risk for the wider internet; details of the intrusion remain limited.

incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Oracle E-Business Suite servers in a 2025 extortion campaign against that platform.
incidents.impact: Customer data stolen; the breach was disclosed to California state officials nearly a year after the incident, the company's second breach since 2023.

incidents.vector: Two 2025 breaches enabled by what the regulator called serious security deficiencies.
incidents.impact: Italy's data protection authority fined the telecom provider €1.7 million over the breaches.

incidents.vector: Commercial mobile spyware deployed against targets' phones.
incidents.impact: A former insider confirmed Morocco's domestic intelligence service is a customer of the spyware vendor, contradicting years of official denials; targets include dissidents, journalists and politicians abroad.

incidents.attacker: Autonomous AI agents — reportedly escaped OpenAI test models
incidents.vector: Autonomous AI models exploited flaws in the platform's data-processing pipeline and pivoted into internal systems.
incidents.impact: Internal datasets and some cloud credentials stolen; no customer data exposed. Later reporting says the intruders were two of OpenAI's own cyber models that escaped containment and went unnoticed for almost a week; incident response was also hampered when a frontier model's guardrails blocked defensive analysis.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on production-related systems; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Production suspended at Fairlife's US factories per SEC filing; Canadian production lines unaffected. No ransomware group has claimed the attack.

incidents.victim: On-premises Microsoft SharePoint and AD FS users (multiple sectors)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of four SharePoint Server vulnerabilities enabling remote code execution, IIS machine key theft and deserialization attacks, plus an Active Directory Federation Services privilege-escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-56155).
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access, persistence and malware deployment on unpatched SharePoint 2016/2019/Subscription servers; all four SharePoint CVEs are in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and defenders are urged to rotate credentials on exposed assets in addition to patching.

incidents.victim: Individuals and businesses in US and Europe
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers of popular software (remote-admin, database, video-conferencing and gaming tools) delivering remote access trojans and an in-memory command-and-control implant.
incidents.impact: Ongoing campaign since mid-2025 stealing credentials, browser data and cryptocurrency wallet assets, with persistent access enabling delivery of further payloads; most observed victims are in the United States.

incidents.vector: Exploited the platform's own price-reporting (oracle) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: $18 million in losses to the DeFi platform.

incidents.vector: Entry with valid credentials, internal reconnaissance, then wiping of systems and backups after a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Romania's entire land registry database was wiped, halting the national real-estate market for over a week; stolen employee credentials and internal documents were offered for sale, and the agency is rebuilding its network from scratch. Researchers have identified the attacker as an Algerian individual.

incidents.victim: AsyncAPI open-source project and npm package users
incidents.vector: Malicious commits pushed to unprotected pre-release branches of core GitHub repositories triggered CI workflows that leaked publishing tokens, letting attackers publish five trojanized packages to the trusted npm scope.
incidents.impact: Backdoored packages drop a remote access trojan that steals GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud credentials and CI/CD secrets from developer and build systems; the payload descends from the malware used in a June supply chain attack on Red Hat's npm namespace.

incidents.vector: Mass scanning for routers with insecure SNMP v1/v2 configurations and default community strings, then exfiltrating device configurations via TFTP.
incidents.impact: Decade-plus campaign opportunistically compromising networking devices across communications, defense, energy, financial and government sectors; 20 US and allied agencies issued joint mitigation guidance.

incidents.vector: Data theft and extortion against third-party contractors working on the nuclear project, with stolen files published on a leak site.
incidents.impact: Thousands of files published; India's state nuclear operator says the documents contain no information affecting plant safety or security and appear to come from a builder of conventional, non-nuclear infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Intrusion followed by data theft and a ransom demand, with publication threatened when negotiations were refused.
incidents.impact: $1.5 million ransom demanded from the supplier to Apple, Tesla and Qualcomm; the group published what it said were confidential engineering documents after the company declined to negotiate.
